faults.d: The rows run to the east wall, so every pick and every put-away goes into a 65 m aisle and back out the same end.
Fast movers sit wherever there was a gap, so pickers and the forklift travel the full length of the aisles.
Forklifts from the doors and pickers from packing share the main aisle and the west entrance to every aisle.
Overflow pallets narrow the main aisle where all traffic meets.
Receiving and shipping share the doors and one staging area. When the forklift falls behind, staging fills and unloading stops.
Every outbound pallet is pushed across the receiving area to reach a door.
Shorter aisles joined by front and back cross-aisles: no dead ends.
The busiest SKUs sit in the front bays closest to packing.
Receiving on the left, shipping on the right: forklifts and pickers mostly keep apart.
Staging has its own lanes in the dock zone, out of the aisles.
Three receiving and two shipping doors, each with its own staging lanes.
Outbound pallets travel under 10 m to their lane.
